45.0.s.en: 1. Holiness and the division of the holy city:

45.0.0.en: 1 Moreover, when ye shall divide by lot the land for inheritance, ye shall offer an oblation unto the LORD, an holy portion of the land: the length shall be the length of five and twenty thousand reeds, and the breadth shall be ten thousand. This shall be holy in all the borders thereof round about. 2 Of this there shall be for the sanctuary five hundred in length, with five hundred in breadth, square round about; and fifty cubits round about for the suburbs thereof. 3 And of this measure shalt thou measure the length of five and twenty thousand, and the breadth of ten thousand: and in it shall be the sanctuary and the most holy place. 4 The holy portion of the land shall be for the priests the ministers of the sanctuary, which shall come near to minister unto the LORD: and it shall be a place for their houses, and an holy place for the sanctuary. 5 And the five and twenty thousand of length, and the ten thousand of breadth shall also the Levites, the ministers of the house, have for themselves, for a possession for twenty chambers. 6 And ye shall appoint the possession of the city five thousand broad, and five and twenty thousand long, over against the oblation of the holy portion: it shall be for the whole house of Israel. 7 And a portion shall be for the prince on the one side and on the other side of the oblation of the holy portion, and of the possession of the city, before the oblation of the holy portion, and before the possession of the city, from the west side westward, and from the east side eastward: and the length shall be over against one of the portions, from the west border unto the east border. 8 In the land shall be his possession in Israel: and my princes shall no more oppress my people; and the rest of the land shall they give to the house of Israel according to their tribes.

45.0.1.en: A. The Lord says: "When ye shall divide by lot the land for inheritance, ye shall offer an oblation unto the LORD, an holy portion of the land... This shall be holy in all the borders thereof round about" [1]. How wondrous is God's love! He promised to give a new land after their return from captivity, and then asks man for a piece of land from what He gave them as an offering from man to God, which becomes a mystery of the sanctification of the whole land. He takes a little of what He gave us as though it were from us, and sanctifies all that we have because of this offering.

45.0.2.en: God accepts this land from us, although the whole earth is the Lord's, and makes it His own possession, a holy house in which He dwells in the midst of His people to sanctify them.

45.0.3.en: This bears a symbolic picture of what was accomplished in the New Testament. The holy portion is the Lord Christ, the only Son of God, who took our body and our nature in Himself so that the Father might receive Him from us as an acceptable and well-pleasing sacrifice of love, and so receive all of us in Him. This Holy One is received on behalf of humanity, and humanity that believes in Him is sanctified through its union with Him and in Him. Therefore St. Cyril the Great says: [We were all in Christ, and the human person in its universality was renewed in Him.] [He bore us in His body, since we were all in Him inasmuch as He was revealed as man.] And Pope Athanasius the Apostolic says: [The Logos Himself had no need of the opening of the gates of heaven... but we were in need of it, we whom He carried in His body.] The Lord Christ was, and still is, the mystery of our sanctification, since He carried us in Himself mystically.

45.0.4.en: The new temple also bears a symbolic picture of what takes place within the human soul, or within the person. If the Holy of Holies represents the heart in which our Lord Jesus Christ dwells, then the temple signifies the body, which is sanctified through the Lord's indwelling in the soul, as the whole temple is sanctified through the Holy of Holies. As for the dimensions of the temple, 500 reeds on every side, they are a memorial of the five wise virgins (Mt 25)... or of the sanctification of the five senses of the body as virgins for our Lord God Jesus. The priests dwelling around the temple point to the holy worship that man offers in Christ Jesus, while the Levites point to the necessity of strict guarding at the doors of the soul and the body together, so that nothing foreign enters us that is unfit for the holy things of God. The king points to the mind, or the holy intellect, which directs affairs according to the will of God, and the people point to the energies of the body and its outward works, as everything in us is sanctified to work for the Kingdom of God.

45.0.5.en: B. The Lord determined the portion of the priests, the Levites, the people and the king, so that no one would encroach on the rights of another, and none would exploit his influence at the expense of his brother... for there is no sanctification without justice and respect for the rights of others.

45.1.s.en: 2. Justice and righteousness in the new city:

45.1.0.en: 9 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Let it suffice you, O princes of Israel: remove violence and spoil, and execute judgment and justice, take away your exactions from my people, saith the Lord GOD. 10 Ye shall have just balances, and a just ephah, and a just bath. 11 The ephah and the bath shall be of one measure, that the bath may contain the tenth part of an homer, and the ephah the tenth part of an homer: the measure thereof shall be after the homer. 12 And the shekel shall be twenty gerahs: twenty shekels, five and twenty shekels, fifteen shekels, shall be your maneh. 13 This is the oblation that ye shall offer; the sixth part of an ephah of an homer of wheat, and ye shall give the sixth part of an ephah of an homer of barley: 14 Concerning the ordinance of oil, the bath of oil, ye shall offer the tenth part of a bath out of the cor, which is an homer of ten baths; for ten baths are an homer: 15 And one lamb out of the flock, out of two hundred, out of the fat pastures of Israel; for a meat offering, and for a burnt offering, and for peace offerings, to make reconciliation for them, saith the Lord GOD. 16 All the people of the land shall give this oblation for the prince in Israel. 17 And it shall be the prince's part to give burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts, and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, in all solemnities of the house of Israel: he shall prepare the sin offering, and the meat offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.

45.2.0.en: The law of the holy land is justice and the absence of injustice or oppression; this is the mark of the soul that receives God within it as the mystery of its sanctification. Therefore the Lord commands those in authority thus: "Remove violence and spoil, and execute judgment and justice, take away your exactions from my people, saith the Lord GOD. Ye shall have just balances, and a just ephah, and a just bath" [10]. For nothing grieves God's heart like injustice and deceit, and nothing gladdens His heart like mercy and justice.

45.2.1.en: This is the constitution of the Church, which finds that in her Christ divine justice has been fulfilled, God's just balances... for He bore our sins and paid the debt that was upon us, and as the Apostle says: "And you, being dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, hath he quickened together with him, having forgiven you all trespasses; Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross; And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it" (Col 2:13-15). We were in the balances upward, and He paid the price, not with words or mere feelings, but He paid His life as the price of our salvation, so divine justice was fulfilled in Him. By this He destroys Satan with his principalities and powers and makes a public example of them, as He destroys injustice and oppression... which is the law of the devil and his hosts.

45.3.0.en: Therefore, after he spoke of the law of justice and the absence of deceit in the offerings, sacrifices and burnt offerings [15], as a symbol of the sacrifice of the Lord Christ in which divine justice is fulfilled!

45.4.0.en: 18 Thus saith the Lord GOD; In the first month, in the first day of the month, thou shalt take a young bullock without blemish, and cleanse the sanctuary: 19 And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering, and put it upon the posts of the house, and upon the four corners of the settle of the altar, and upon the posts of the gate of the inner court. 20 And so thou shalt do the seventh day of the month for every one that erreth, and for him that is simple: so shall ye reconcile the house. 21 In the first month, in the fourteenth day of the month, ye shall have the passover, a feast of seven days; unleavened bread shall be eaten. 22 And upon that day shall the prince prepare for himself and for all the people of the land a bullock for a sin offering. 23 And seven days of the feast he shall prepare a burnt offering to the LORD, seven bullocks and seven rams without blemish daily the seven days; and a kid of the goats daily for a sin offering. 24 And he shall prepare a meat offering of an ephah for a bullock, and an ephah for a ram, and an hin of oil for an ephah. 25 In the seventh month, in the fifteenth day of the month, shall he do the like in the feast of the seven days, according to the sin offering, according to the burnt offering, and according to the meat offering, and according to the oil.

45.4.1.en: If the foundation of the Church is the holiness that has become ours in the Holy Christ, and her law is the justice fulfilled in His sacrifice, then her mark is "joy" in the Lord. Therefore God speaks to them of continual feasts... for the life of the Church is a perpetual "feast" and a heavenly joy that the events of the world cannot take away.

45.4.2.en: Christianity is not gloom, nor weariness, nor bitterness, but in its essence an inner joy realized as the fruit of the Holy Spirit (Gal 5:23) through its constant leaning on the breast of the Lord Christ, its Head, who conquers and remains conquering in us (Rev 6:2). In Him the Church sees the heavens opened, and she sits at the right hand of the Father through her union with His only Son... This is the secret of her perpetual joy: constant victory and the opening of the heavens before her through her union with God in Christ Jesus!

45.4.3.en: Here the feasts began with the feast of the beginning of the year [18], on the first day of the first month, then the Passover [21], and in the next chapter he spoke of the sabbaths and the perpetual feast (the daily morning and evening burnt offerings). All of these in Christ Jesus are our continual feast: He is the beginning of our new life (the new year), He is our Passover who was sacrificed for us (1 Cor 5:7), He is our true Sabbath, that is, the mystery of our rest, and He is the daily feast in which is the mystery of our joy morning and evening every day. We have already spoken of the Jewish feasts as a symbol of the Christian feast in our study of the Book of Numbers.

45.4.5.en: * Declare within me, in Your temple, Your law:

45.4.7.en: *What is Your law, O Holy One, but holiness?!

45.4.8.en: In You my body is sanctified, the new earth!

45.4.9.en: And in You my soul is sanctified, the new heaven!

45.4.10.en: And by You my gifts are sanctified, the new Levites!

45.4.11.en: And by You my mind is sanctified, the new king!

45.4.12.en: You are the sanctifier of soul, body and spirit!

45.4.13.en: * O Truth in whom there is no falsehood!

45.4.15.en: Grant me the constitution of truth and justice within me!

45.4.16.en: Remove from me all falsehood and injustice!

45.4.17.en: *Your indwelling in my depths removes sorrow; Your presence is a joyful Kingdom!

45.4.18.en: Your being turns my life into an unceasing hymn of praise!

46.0.s.en: 1. The manner of entering the temple:

46.0.0.en: 1 Thus saith the Lord GOD; The gate of the inner court that looketh toward the east shall be shut the six working days; but on the sabbath it shall be opened, and in the day of the new moon it shall be opened. 2 And the prince shall enter by the way of the porch of that gate without, and shall stand by the post of the gate, and the priests shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he shall worship at the threshold of the gate: then he shall go forth; but the gate shall not be shut until the evening. 3 Likewise the people of the land shall worship at the door of this gate before the LORD in the sabbaths and in the new moons. 4 And the burnt offering that the prince shall offer unto the LORD in the sabbath day shall be six lambs without blemish, and a ram without blemish. 5 And the meat offering shall be an ephah for a ram, and the meat offering for the lambs as he shall be able to give, and an hin of oil to an ephah. 6 And in the day of the new moon it shall be a young bullock without blemish, and six lambs, and a ram: they shall be without blemish. 7 And he shall prepare a meat offering, an ephah for a bullock, and an ephah for a ram, and for the lambs according as his hand shall attain unto, and an hin of oil to an ephah. 8 And when the prince shall enter, he shall go in by the way of the porch of that gate, and he shall go forth by the way thereof. 9 But when the people of the land shall come before the LORD in the solemn feasts, he that entereth in by the way of the north gate to worship shall go out by the way of the south gate; and he that entereth by the way of the south gate shall go forth by the way of the north gate: he shall not return by the way of the gate whereby he came in, but shall go forth over against it. 10 And the prince in the midst of them, when they go in, shall go in; and when they go forth, shall go forth. 11 And in the feasts and in the solemnities the meat offering shall be an ephah to a bullock, and an ephah to a ram, and to the lambs as he is able to give, and an hin of oil to an ephah. 12 Now when the prince shall prepare a voluntary burnt offering or peace offerings voluntarily unto the LORD, one shall then open him the gate that looketh toward the east, and he shall prepare his burnt offering and his peace offerings, as he did on the sabbath day: then he shall go forth; and after his going forth one shall shut the gate. 13 Thou shalt daily prepare a burnt offering unto the LORD of a lamb of the first year without blemish: thou shalt prepare it every morning. 14 And thou shalt prepare a meat offering for it every morning, the sixth part of an ephah, and the third part of an hin of oil, to temper with the fine flour; a meat offering continually by a perpetual ordinance unto the LORD. 15 Thus shall they prepare the lamb, and the meat offering, and the oil, every morning for a continual burnt offering.

46.0.1.en: In this section he presented to us the manner of the king's entry and the people's entry into the temple, and their going out also, and the burnt offerings and sacrifices that the king and the people offer on the sabbaths and feasts, and he also spoke of the daily burnt offerings. It is noticed that what is mentioned here was not fulfilled literally after the people's return from the Babylonian captivity and the re-establishment of the temple with its worship, but they kept to the Law of Moses, as though what is mentioned here is not meant in a literal sense but in the symbolic meaning in the Messianic age.

46.0.2.en: The most important laws mentioned here are:

46.0.3.en: A. The east gate of the inner court is closed six days, and on the Sabbath alone, as on the day of the new moon, it is opened for the king to enter by it, and by it also to go out; but the people neither enter by it nor go out by it... it is reserved for the king. We have said that this gate refers to the womb of the Virgin, in which the King of kings entered and became incarnate, and from which He came forth.

46.0.4.en: If the Lord entered humanity once and became man, He still enters our life shining like the sun from the east gate; He comes to us to make our days sabbaths (rest) and feasts. He shines in us with His light, so that darkness has no place in us, but we are enlightened continually, rejoicing in His perpetual dwelling in us, as the Lord Himself assured His disciples shortly before His ascension: "Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world" (Mt 28:20).

46.0.5.en: The people enter by the north and south gates; whoever enters from the north walks toward the south to worship and does not return to the gate by which he entered but goes out by the south gate, and likewise whoever enters by the south gate walks toward the north to worship and does not turn back to the south but goes out by the opposite north gate. Some have seen in this arrangement the preservation of the temple's quiet and the avoidance of confusion in traffic within it, especially at the feasts when the numbers are very large; but I think that this arrangement presents to us a picture of the life of the Christian who walks inside the temple to worship God and does not turn back again! It is a picture of walking uprightly in the direction that has become his through the new life of the Church, without turning aside from the Christian way of faith.

46.0.6.en: B. The east gate of the inner court is opened on the Sabbath all day until evening, as though God enters into our inner life, shining in our depths as long as it is day. He enters us to make our hearts in a perpetual "rest (Sabbath)."

46.0.7.en: The scholar Origen speaks of the celebration of the Sabbath, saying:

46.0.8.en: [What is the celebration of the Sabbath but what the Apostle said: "There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God" (Heb 4:9), that is, He fulfills the law of the Sabbath. Let the people of God leave the Jewish form of the Sabbath, and let us see what we should do as a Christian order on the day of the Sabbath. We must not engage in any worldly activity or temporal work... so that we are free for spiritual exercises: going to church and listening to the divine readings and sermons, contemplating heavenly things, being concerned for the life to come, thinking of the coming judgment, and being concerned not with present visible things but with the future invisible realities. This is the keeping of the Sabbath for the Christian.]

46.0.9.en: [Let us search deeply for the true Sabbath. It means working in heaven; for we do not see that the words of the book of Genesis: "And he (the Lord) rested on the seventh day (the Sabbath) from all his work which he had made" (Gen 2:2) were fulfilled literally on the seventh day, nor are they fulfilled today. For God works continually; there is no Sabbath on which the Lord does not work. There is no day on which He does not make His sun to rise on the evil and the good, or does not send rain on the just and the unjust (Mt 5:45). He "maketh grass to grow upon the mountains" (Ps 147:8), He "woundeth, and bindeth up" (Job 5:18), showing that in this age there is no Sabbath day on which the Lord rests from governing the world and caring for the destinies of the human race.]

46.0.10.en: We have already seen in our study of the Book of Exodus that the Lord Christ is the true Sabbath; in Him the Father rests, finding us in Him justified and sanctified to Him, and in Him we too rest, as we enter by Him into the bosom of the Father, the place of our rest. He is the Sabbath of the Father and the Sabbath of the believers, the mystery of true rest!

46.0.11.en: C. The gate is also opened on the first day of the month [1] and remains open all day. Perhaps he meant by this "the day of the new moon," which had its sanctity among the Jews like the Sabbaths, feasts and appointed times (1 Chr 23:13; 2:4; Ezra 3:5; Col 2:16); they used to blow the trumpets (Ps 81:3), celebrate it in their houses (Prov 7:20), and worship the Lord on it (Isa 66:23).

46.0.12.en: The scholar Origen comments on this celebration, saying: [The celebration of the feast of the new moon means the approach of the moon to the sun and its union with it... The feast is held at the changing of the moon, when it comes very near to the sun and is closely united with "the Sun of righteousness" (Mal 4:2), who is Christ. If the moon means His Church, full of light, which is joined and united with Him strongly, as the Apostle says: "But he that is joined unto the Lord is one spirit" (1 Cor 6:17), then she celebrates the feast of the new moon as she becomes new by putting off the old man and putting on the new man, "which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness" (Eph 4:24). Thus she is worthy to celebrate the feast of renewal, the feast of the new moon.]

46.1.0.en: D. The perpetual feast: He says, "Thou shalt daily prepare a burnt offering unto the LORD of a lamb of the first year without blemish: thou shalt prepare it every morning. And thou shalt prepare a meat offering for it every morning... a meat offering continually by a perpetual ordinance unto the LORD" [13-14].

46.1.1.en: The scholar Origen says: [The first feast of the Lord is the perpetual feast. Truly, the offering of sacrifices every morning and evening continually without interruption is required. So also in the legislation of the feasts (in the Book of Numbers) the Lord did not begin with the feast of the Passover, the feast of unleavened bread or the feast of the holy offering, nor with any other of the feasts prescribed, but decreed that the first feast is the feast of the perpetual sacrifice. He wants the one who reaches perfection and holiness not to have days that are feasts and others that are not feasts to God, for the righteous man celebrates a perpetual feast.]

46.1.2.en: Thus speaks the scholar Origen, known for his churchly spirit, who without doubt rejoiced in the feasts of the Church throughout the days of the year, but who finds a feast in every day he lives with God. For the Christian's feasts never cease, as he enters into heavenly joy and continually tastes the pledge of the eternal Kingdom.

46.2.s.en: 2. The gifts of the prince or king:

46.2.0.en: 16 Thus saith the Lord GOD; If the prince give a gift unto any of his sons, the inheritance thereof shall be his sons'; it shall be their possession by inheritance. 17 But if he give a gift of his inheritance to one of his servants, then it shall be his to the year of liberty; after it shall return to the prince: but his inheritance shall be his sons' for them. 18 Moreover the prince shall not take of the people's inheritance by oppression, to thrust them out of their possession; but he shall give his sons inheritance out of his own possession: that my people be not scattered every man from his possession.

46.2.1.en: God wanted to preserve the right of the king and his family, and also the right of the people, and He determined the portion of each in the previous chapter. But if the king wishes to give a gift from his inheritance to someone, God distinguished between two cases: if the one who enjoys the gift is a son of the king, the gift remains an inheritance for him and his children without end, because the land remains in the possession of the royal family; but if the gift is to one of the people, it remains his until the year of liberty, when the gift returns to the king. By this the inheritance of the royal family does not leak to the people, nor the inheritance of the people to the royal family, since it is not lawful for the king to seize or acquire anything of the people's inheritance.

46.2.2.en: Perhaps in this too is a symbolic picture of the inheritance in the New Testament, for there is a difference between the son and the servant: the son inherits and possesses for ever, while the servant enjoys temporary blessings. Therefore, if we wish to become heirs of God, and joint heirs with Christ the only Son, there is no room for eternal inheritance except through enjoying the new birth, or receiving the Spirit of adoption as sons of God.

46.3.0.en: 19 After he brought me through the entry, which was at the side of the gate, into the holy chambers of the priests, which looked toward the north: and, behold, there was a place on the two sides westward. 20 Then said he unto me, This is the place where the priests shall boil the trespass offering and the sin offering, where they shall bake the meat offering; that they bear them not out into the utter court, to sanctify the people. 21 Then he brought me forth into the utter court, and caused me to pass by the four corners of the court; and, behold, in every corner of the court there was a court. 22 In the four corners of the court there were courts joined of forty cubits long and thirty broad: these four corners were of one measure. 23 And there was a row of building round about in them, round about them four, and it was made with boiling places under the rows round about. 24 Then said he unto me, These are the places of them that boil, where the ministers of the house shall boil the sacrifice of the people.

46.3.1.en: The Lord appointed places for the priests to cook in their chambers in the inner court, and also appointed other places at the edges of the outer court, in the four corners... and appointed places for baking.

46.3.2.en: How great is the difference between one who enters the inner court and one who remains in the outer court... yet no one is left hungry once he has entered into fellowship with the Lord Christ. He gives everyone of His holy things... but it is fitting for us to enter always and without ceasing toward the inside, so that we may have a fellowship of inner life with Him and be satisfied from His holy things.

46.3.3.en: You are my rest and my perpetual feast!

46.3.4.en: * How wondrous are Your laws that You laid down for my heart, which is Your temple!

46.3.5.en: Do not allow those who enter it except to walk uprightly!

46.3.6.en: You are the Truth who does not admit deviation!

46.3.7.en: * You gave me the law of Your weekly and yearly feasts: they are the sabbaths of rest and the feasts of joy.

46.3.8.en: You are my sabbaths... You are my rest, O Savior!

46.3.9.en: You are my joy and my perpetual feast, O Giver of the resurrection!

46.3.10.en: You are my unceasing hymn of praise!

46.3.11.en: * You gave the king his rights and obligations, and the people also!

46.3.12.en: No one may seize from another or exploit him!

46.3.13.en: Keep my mind by Your Holy Spirit, that it may reign in justice and not corrupt my life!

46.3.14.en: * In Your care for Your priests You commanded places for cooking and baking.

46.3.15.en: You are wondrous, O heavenly Bread, for You seek the satisfaction of all!
